subject: pugs with allergies
one_liner: A conversational model trained on the allergy records of 4,100 pugs, so your pug can finally explain itself.
brand_voice_notes: Veterinary clinic officialdom. Every claim arrives as settled fact with a number bolted to it. Nothing is ever framed as fun or cute, least of all the pugs. The product is expensive, extremely slow, and confident in findings that help no one. Sentences are short and administrative. Prices are stated once and never justified.

hero.h1: Your pug has been saying something for six years.
hero.sub: Brachy records ambient respiratory audio from the dog bed and returns a ranked household allergen report. First findings in nine weeks.

features.title: Wheeze transcription
features.blurb: A calibrated microphone in the bed captures fourteen hours of nightly breathing. Brachy renders it as complete English sentences, punctuated, in your pug's registered voice profile. Grammar is inferred. Tone is not.

features.title: Elimination protocol
features.blurb: We remove one object from your home per week and observe. The protocol runs forty weeks and does not accept substitutions. Most households finish with no sofa and no conclusive finding.

features.title: Veterinary correspondence
features.blurb: Brachy emails your actual veterinarian on your pug's behalf, cites its own report, and does not stand down. Average thread runs thirty-one messages before the clinic stops replying.

demo_screen_concept: A two-pane intake console titled 'Intake 0441'. Left pane: the Household Allergen Panel, a scrollable list of nine domestic items (velvet sofa, hallway runner, the brother, oat-based kibble, lavender diffuser, wool throw, the mail, radiator dust, seasonal pollen) each with a severity bar, a confidence percentage, and an 'eliminate' toggle. Toggling recalculates a live Household Load gauge out of 100 and appends a timestamped line to the protocol ledger. Right pane: a chat transcript between owner and pug, with the pug's messages rendered by Brachy behind a small circular pug avatar and a per-message confidence badge. Below the transcript, a row of canned prompts the owner can send ('How is the hallway?', 'Explain the sofa', 'Are you sure about my brother?'), each appending a new deadpan reply. Three tabs across the top switch between Transcript, Protocol Ledger, and Vet Thread, the last showing a stalled thirty-one-message email chain with a real veterinary clinic that has stopped responding.

images.rationale: Full budget of 4 spent. Hero taken: the enamel-signage direction is built on a real physical room, so a documentary shot of a pug on terrazzo in front of bolted cobalt panels does work the CSS cannot, and it anchors the palette. Dedicated demo assets skipped because the demo screen is a chat transcript plus a ledger, which is document-shaped and gets no photograph; the demo borrows headshot-1 as the pug's circular chat avatar instead. Remaining 3 slots went to testimonial headshots, one per named pug, each shot against a different colour from the palette so the testimonial row reads as a records wall.

items.prompt: Editorial documentary photograph of a single pug sitting upright on a terrazzo floor in the waiting room of an old municipal veterinary clinic. The pug is the sole focal subject, centered, facing the camera with a flat resigned expression, slightly watery eyes. Behind it, out of focus, a wall of deep cobalt blue #1D4E89 porcelain-enamel panels and a strip of enamel green #2E7D5B, chipped at the edges, bolted to the wall. Floor is warm cream terrazzo #EDE7DA flecked with small cobalt and green stone chips. Cool institutional daylight from a high window, flat and even, no drama, no warm golden glow. Muted restrained palette of cream, cobalt, enamel green and grey steel. Shot on film, medium format, natural grain, shallow depth of field. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no signage lettering, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens, no user interface elements.
items.judge: pass. Subject correct and deadpan. Palette is the design direction almost literally: cobalt enamel panels with visible bolt heads, a chipped green rail, cream terrazzo speckled in cobalt and green. Flat institutional daylight, no golden-hour AI tell. No text artifacts.

design_direction.style: Vitreous enamel signage over terrazzo, veterinary waiting-room daylight mode. The page is staged as the interior signage of a municipal animal clinic that has been in the same building since 1954: porcelain-enamelled steel plaques bolted to a terrazzo wall, with chipped edges, rolled borders, and one plaque per statement. There is no glass, no backdrop blur, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no newsprint or riso misregistration, no ground-glass amber, no leaded came, no moulded plastic, no plaster, no engraved guilloche, no pharmaceutical fold, and no galvanized zinc. Four motifs carry the whole page. (1) The enamel plaque: every card is a solid-colour panel with a 3px inset white keyline set 4px from the edge, a 4px corner radius, and a 1px darker outer rule, sitting on the terrazzo ground with a hard 2px down shadow at 22 percent black and zero blur, because enamel is flat steel and does not float. (2) The chip: one 8px irregular notch of exposed grey steel (#9AA0A0) at a single corner of each major plaque, never more than one per plaque, never on buttons. (3) The terrazzo ground: the page background is #EDE7DA carrying a fixed, non-animated speckle of small irregular flecks in #C3BBA8, #1D4E89 at 12 percent, and #2E7D5B at 10 percent, generated as a repeating radial-gradient field, dense enough to read as stone at arm's length and never as noise texture. (4) The bolt: a 7px circle in #9AA0A0 with a 1px #6E7474 ring and a single 1px darker slot line, placed at the two upper corners of every plaque, always exactly two, because these signs are screwed to a wall. Headings are Alfa Slab One, a single heavy slab weight, set in sentence case at large sizes and never letterspaced, the way a sign painter cuts one size of stencil and lives with it. Body and all sub-headings are Rubik, 17px, line-height 1.65, weights 400 and 500 only. Every figure, price, percentage, confidence score, and ledger timestamp is Rubik with tabular figures at 500, because this clinic counts things. Rules between sections are 2px solid #1D4E89, full bleed, with an 8px gap of terrazzo above and below. Cobalt #1D4E89 is the institutional colour and carries all primary plaques and CTAs; enamel green #2E7D5B appears only on confirmations, severity bars, and the second pricing tier; the two never touch without a white keyline between them.
design_direction.archetype: Consumer AI assistant product page issued as municipal veterinary clinic signage: a wall of bolted enamel plaques over terrazzo, read top to bottom, each section one plaque, with the intake console reached through a plaque that looks like a door sign.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Enamel does not bounce. Toggles snap between two states in 120ms with no overshoot. Section entrances are a 200ms opacity lift and nothing else, never a translate, so the page photographs identically with and without JS. Hover on a plaque darkens its fill by 6 percent and deepens the hard shadow from 2px to 3px, with no lift. The single sustained motion in the build is the Household Load needle in the demo, which settles over 400ms on a slight overshoot like a mechanical gauge, and it is the only easing curve in the project that is not linear.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed terrazzo ground. The hero is one oversized cobalt enamel plaque occupying roughly 62 percent of the viewport width, flush left with a wide terrazzo gutter on the right holding a small stacked spec column (INTAKE / PANEL / CYCLE / RESULT) in tabular Rubik caps at 11px. The h1 sits in Alfa Slab One at clamp(2.6rem, 6vw, 4.6rem) in #EDE7DA on the cobalt, with the inset white keyline running behind it. The photograph sits below the plaque as a full-width 16:9 band with a 2px cobalt rule above and below it, never cropped into a circle or rounded. The primary CTA is a green enamel plaque with its own keyline and two bolts, placed half-overlapping the bottom edge of the cobalt plaque so it reads as a second sign screwed over the first.
